additional_concerns: All 12 required pairs are retained, including both historical CONTEXT pairs. NOT_APPLICABLE correspondence is limited to each exact typed question; it neither rejects the supported claim nor authorizes pruning it.

The XML and web-form claims incorrectly describe footnote 3 as missing. Unit da12aecad4e68.u30.3569 states: "Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission." Markers appear on XML and PDF in da12aecad4e68.u4.1003 and da12aecad4e68.u5.1078. The XML permission is supported, but its listed conditions are incomplete if interpreted as jointly sufficient without e-Cert.

The four declared dependencies missing.39ffa0d54487ee68b17a36b8, missing.da4d23ff33f664a99e4bf8cc, missing.f5f807738efdd34996b25ddc and missing.1557ee52aade13863ae98bda each have source_hash null and no supplied description binding the ID to a particular authority. Their contents and availability cannot be established. No AVAILABLE assessment treats these dependencies as resolved, and no semantic identity has been invented for them.

Missing materials or interpretive support include the separately provided JFIU XML schema, the prescribed PDF form or specification, operational instructions establishing how an e-Cert meets the requirement, an explicit governing-timezone basis, and any subsequently issued resubmission guidance. Their relevance differs: the schema and PDF specification affect concrete classifications; resubmission guidance is not shown to be a prerequisite to the duty stated in da12aecad4e68.u28.3334.

The supplied source retains competing temporal formulations. Unit da12aecad4e68.u3.811 says "With effect from 2 February 2026", while da12aecad4e68.u13.2131 says "upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026" and da12aecad4e68.u28.3334 says "following its implementation". The calendar-date candidate node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 includes pre-9:00am events on that date, whereas the launch-instant candidates do not. Neither interpretation is conclusively selected by these scoped checks; treatment of the exact launch instant also remains an interpretive choice.

The blackout text must remain distinct. Unit da12aecad4e68.u12.1941 states: "for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;". Contact alone does not establish a completed STR submission, but the text also does not establish that every urgent contact is incapable of transmitting one. An actual pre-9:00am submission on 2 February 2026 is a discriminating case for the competing temporal interpretations.

The event candidates have a substantive scope difference. Node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb uses "Scope: the fact licensed_firm" and places submitted_to_jfiu in the result. The other event candidates place actual STR filing within scope. For a known licensed firm and a known non-filing event, the former can return FALSE while the others return OUT_OF_SCOPE. For uncertain event classification, scope handling can also differ from conjunction handling. This is not resolved by renaming facts.

The compliance candidates explicitly distinguish XML format from schema conformity. Node.c8bd87cfd64bba8762d9b3a0 states: "xml_submission: The assessed submission is an STR in XML format; this fact alone does not establish compliance with the separately provided schema. (Boolean)". Node.e527b70be44a95d97a2e5ae5 states: "submission_uses_xml: The STR was submitted in Extensible Markup Language format. This fact does not assert conformity with the separately provided JFIU XML schema. (Boolean format observation for one submission event)". Their XML branches can therefore pass without schema conformity. That is an unsupported permission if their result is presented as overall XML submission compliance; whether schema compliance belongs within the selected method control or a separate control must remain explicit.

Unit da12aecad4e68.u14.2439 also requires firms intending XML submission to "liaise with it as soon as possible to arrange a technical test to ensure a smooth transition." This firm-level transitional obligation should be retained separately. The source does not expressly make successful completion of a test an additional per-submission Boolean condition.

Node.e527b70be44a95d97a2e5ae5 defines "hongkong_post_ecert_supplied_for_submission: A Hongkong Post e-Cert was supplied or used for this particular XML or PDF submission in the manner required for that submission. Mere possession of a certificate is insufficient. The operational manner must be established before this fact can be supplied. (Boolean certificate condition for one submission event)". Footnote 3 establishes a requirement but does not specify supplying, attaching, signing or another operational manner. This predicate may be a faithful operationalization, but the supplied authority does not establish it. Missing operational support should retain uncertainty rather than turn an unverified interpretation into a failed submission.

The compliance formulas' web-form branch is supported by the option's lack of a footnote 3 marker. This does not establish exemption from every possible certificate or platform-access requirement. Conversely, imposing the XML/PDF footnote on all web-form submissions would add a restriction not established by the retained text.

The history candidate supplies existential assessment externally: "Result: the fact report_has_postlaunch_other_channel_submission". The formula does not inspect events or establish history completeness. TRUE requires a qualifying event; FALSE requires sufficient history to exclude one. Later resubmission may address the duty but does not negate the historical existence asked about here.

Each representation states: "A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch." A conflict concerning XML, PDF or e-Cert can therefore block evaluation even when a web-form branch would otherwise establish the selected control. This is a declared runtime evidence policy, not an additional legal condition; it must not be reported as legal noncompliance.

These assessments inspect the supplied representations, not running implementations or actual submission evidence. AVAILABLE authority for a narrow permission or context claim does not establish correct interpretation of every candidate dependency, and a supported claim outside the question does not establish executable preservation.
